**Problem.** Determine the abelianization of $\pi_1(\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus k)$, where $k$ is a knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

---

**Proof.**

The abelianization of a group $G$ is, by definition, the quotient $G/[G,G]$, which is naturally isomorphic to the first homology group $H_1$ of any space whose fundamental group is $G$. Hence

$$\pi_1(\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus k)^{\mathrm{ab}} \;\cong\; H_1(\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus k;\,\mathbb{Z}).$$

It remains to compute $H_1(\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus k;\,\mathbb{Z})$.

A knot is, by definition, an embedding $k: S^1 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$, so as a topological space $k \cong S^1$. We apply **Alexander duality**. In its reduced form, for any nonempty compact locally contractible subspace $A \subset S^n$:

$$\tilde{H}_i(S^n \setminus A;\,\mathbb{Z}) \;\cong\; \tilde{H}^{n-i-1}(A;\,\mathbb{Z}), \qquad i \ge 0.$$

We pass from $\mathbb{R}^3$ to $S^3$ via one-point compactification. The knot $k \subset \mathbb{R}^3 \subset S^3$ is a compact, locally contractible subset of $S^3$, and the point at infinity lies in the complement, so

$$\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus k \;\cong\; S^3 \setminus (k \cup \{\infty\}).$$

Since $\infty$ is an isolated point of the removed set, the complement $S^3 \setminus (k \cup \{\infty\})$ has the same reduced homology as $S^3 \setminus k$ (removing an isolated point from the complement does not affect reduced homology; equivalently, $S^3 \setminus (k \cup \{\infty\}) \simeq S^3 \setminus k$ up to a disjoint basepoint issue that vanishes upon taking reduced homology). Concretely, $S^3 \setminus k$ is connected (a knot complement is always connected), and $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus k$ is an open subset of it differing by a single point, so the reduced homology agrees. Thus:

$$\tilde{H}_1(S^3 \setminus k;\,\mathbb{Z}) \;\cong\; \tilde{H}^{3-1-1}(k;\,\mathbb{Z}) \;=\; \tilde{H}^1(k;\,\mathbb{Z}).$$

Since $k \cong S^1$:

$$\tilde{H}^1(S^1;\,\mathbb{Z}) \;\cong\; H^1(S^1;\,\mathbb{Z}) \;\cong\; \mathbb{Z},$$

where the first isomorphism uses $\tilde{H}^1 = H^1$ for a connected space (reduced cohomology only differs from unreduced in degree $0$).

Therefore

$$H_1(\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus k;\,\mathbb{Z}) \;\cong\; \mathbb{Z},$$

and consequently

$$\boxed{\pi_1(\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus k)^{\mathrm{ab}} \;\cong\; \mathbb{Z}.}$$

**Remark on the generator.** The generator of this $\mathbb{Z}$ is represented by a meridian of the knot — a small loop linking $k$ once. This is consistent with the Wirtinger presentation of the knot group: every generator is a meridian conjugate to every other, and every relation is of the form $x_i x_j x_i^{-1} = x_k$, which becomes trivial upon abelianization, leaving all generators equal to a single meridian of infinite order. The longitude (which commutes with the meridian in the abelianization) is trivial in $H_1$ because it has linking number zero with $k$ and bounds a Seifert surface in the complement. Hence the abelianization is freely generated by the meridian class, giving $\mathbb{Z}$, independent of the knot type.

### PROOF COMPLETE
